newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai bourse orders re-audit of annual reports.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai bourse orders re-audit of annual reports.

text.p: The Shanghai stock exchange has ordered a re-examination of the 1996 annual reports so far issued by listed firms to ensure they comply with new disclosure requirements, the Shanghai Securities News said on Saturday.
The newspaper said the order followed Friday's directive from the China Securities Regulatory Commission warning of harsh punishments for companies that included false information in their reports.
The newspaper said the Shanghai stock exchange had decided to strengthen supervision of the annual reports.
"Staff have been organised to undertake a full re-audit of all indicators to ensure the full implementation of the directive," the newspaper said.

The newspaper said in a commentary that quite a few problems had been found in the annual reports issued so far, partly because of the large number of newly-listed companies reporting this year for the first time.

All Chinese firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges are required by exchange rules to post their 1996 annual results before April 30. About 100 of the more than 500 firms have so far done so.
